name: CI Admission and Fallback Triage
summary: Distinguish hosted CI job-admission failures from actual test failures, and produce exact-revision verification evidence through a trusted bounded alternative.
problem: A red CI badge may mean billing, runner allocation or permissions prevented the job from starting; treating it as failed tests or bypassing it with unpinned local checks can corrupt release decisions.
coreOutcomes: Runner-admission, environment and source-test failures separated
Exact revision and intended job matrix pinned before fallback
Bounded trusted alternative execution with truthful parity limitations
Protected release gates remain explicit instead of silently bypassed
requirements: Read access to original CI run, job annotations and repository revision
A trusted controlled executor with the required platform and toolchain
A documented equivalent test command set and reproducible fixture
Explicit project spending and source-permission boundaries
boundaries: A local green suite is not a green hosted GitHub Actions check
An executor with a different OS or architecture does not prove platform parity
Never change billing or bypass required repository checks without authority
A job that never started provides no evidence about test correctness
Alternative CI results must be bound to the exact candidate commit
